title: Classical adic strata for the raw rational constructible heart
statement:
Fix a prime power $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell
e p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, as in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $M\in\operatorname{Sh}_c(T,\Qlb)$ in the raw/common-stage heart of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex; def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure]. There are a finite coefficient field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$, a representative $M_E$ in the raw $E$-heart, and a finite partition $T=\coprod_
u T_
u$ by reduced locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification], such that each $M|_{T_
u}$ is the realization, by the lisse realization functor of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization], of a classical lisse $\Qlb$-sheaf of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. More precisely, at the same $E$ each restriction has a lisse integral lattice $L_
u$ over $B_{E,T_
u}=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_{T_
u}$ whose localization realizes $M_E|_{T_
u}$. The reductions $L_{
u,n}$ are finite locally free sheaves on $(T_
u)_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $L_{
u,n+1}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1}}\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\cong L_{
u,n}$.

The comparison from the sf raw heart to the PBC raw heart is the identity-induced $J$ of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison]; it identifies their cohomological halves and geometric fibres. At a finite stage its continuous module realization, the equivalence of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], has coefficient ring $B_{E,T}[1/\varpi_E]$. The continuous and pulled-back condensed coefficient rings, integrally as well as rationally, are identified with these displayed rings by their finite-quotient projections. The resulting classical lisse realizations are fully faithful on maps, identify adic point fibres and iterated geometric-Frobenius point transports, and commute with further locally closed restriction and finite coefficient extension. In particular, if $T=Y_0	imes_{k_0}k$ for a separated finite-type $Y_0$, and $M$ has a Weil structure, then on any further locally closed piece defined over $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}$ inside one $T_
u$, its iterated Weil map comes from a classical lisse Weil isomorphism. No Frobenius stability of the initial partition or of the integral lattices is required.

When $T=(Y_0	imes_{k_0}k)_{\mathrm{red}}$ for a separated finite-type $Y_0$, there is one finite $k_m/k_0$ and a finite reduced closed chain $Z_0=(Y_0	imes_{k_0}k_m)_{\mathrm{red}}\supset\cdots\supset Z_t=\varnothing$ whose open differences are finite disjoint unions of nonempty smooth geometrically connected affine $k_m$-schemes of constant nonnegative dimension, with all inclusions defined over $k_m$. Their geometric base changes refine the displayed classical-lisse partition, and the restrictions of $M$ remain classical lisse with the same normalized pullback and coefficient comparisons. A zero-dimensional piece is $\operatorname{Spec}k_m$.

source.place: Paragraphs 6-7: constructing the lisse adapted partition before smooth affine refinement; raw-heart, continuous-coefficient and normalized integral-system identifications expanded in returned Steps 8-9. Returned Step 10: simultaneous finite-field frontier refinement preserving the normalized lisse systems.

proof.text: The schemes to which we apply the comparisons are allowed: $T$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied over the spectrum of the field $k$, and has finite dimension by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. The same holds for its locally closed reduced strata, which are again finite type over $k$; $\ell$ is invertible since $\ell\ne p$. At every finite coefficient stage the integral categories in the sf and PBC conventions are the same full category, with the same completed ring and cohomology sheaves, by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. The equivalence $J$ in [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] is the identity on this category and its localized arrows. The sf integral halves in [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] are the vanishing classes of the cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^r$ over the completed coefficient sheaf, and the PBC integral halves of [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure] are the vanishing classes of the same ambient cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^i$ over the same completed ring; so the two integral halves are the same classes of the common integral category. The sf rational halves in [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] and the PBC rational halves in [prop-weil-localized-tstructure] are the isomorphism closures of these integral halves. Thus $J$ carries each half onto the corresponding half. Its common-stage extension does the same, since it identifies the finite-stage inclusions and scalar transitions.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3) and Proposition 6.8.14(2); identity comparison and standard-pair definitions in the cited nodes

proof.text: Use $J$ to view $M$ in the PBC common-stage heart. By [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres], the common-stage heart consists of objects isomorphic to a pair $(E,N_E)$ with $N_E$ in the finite-stage rational heart. Choose such a pair; transporting back by $J_{T,E}^{-1}$ gives $M_E$ in the raw sf $E$-heart and an isomorphism $(E,M_E)\simeq M$. We fix this $E$ for the construction of all strata and lattices. Apply [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] to $N_E=J_{T,E}M_E$: its image is a constructible sheaf $F$ of modules over $E_T=B_{E,T}[1/\varpi_E]$, in degree zero. This uses the equivalence's asserted identification of hearts, rather than assuming an arbitrary integral representative is a sheaf.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2), with Proposition 6.8.11(3); common-stage heart formulation in lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres

proof.text: We first compare the actual completed pullbacks, with their normalizations. For any $h:V\to W$ under consideration, the sf completed pullback in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the PBC completed pullback in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] apply finite-level pullback to the reductions of the same integral representative, with the same quotient transitions, then realize that whole tower. The integral identity equivalence identifies these input diagrams. Applying the derived-limit functor to this identity gives the comparison. The resolution independence, composition and coefficient comparisons are supplied by the whole-diagram realization of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization].

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2, Proposition 6.8.4 and Remark 6.8.15; Stacks Tag 099N, proetale.tex lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (2),(5), with the cited whole-tower normalization

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$, $\varpi=\varpi_E$. The coefficient identifications in [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] give $B_{E,W}=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_W$ and $B_{E,W}[1/\varpi]=E_W$ as continuous integral and rational coefficient sheaves, with the specified finite-quotient normalizations. By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations], the pulled-back condensed $A$ and $E$ rings identify with these continuous-function sheaves, and the inclusion $A\to E$ is respected. The totally disconnected hypothesis here holds: residue classes modulo $\varpi^n$ separate distinct points of $A$, and their scaled translates are clopen balls separating distinct points of $E$. Consequently the composite integral comparison has its $n$th projection equal to reduction modulo $\varpi^n$, and its rational comparison is the localization of this same map. We use these maps, not independently chosen ring isomorphisms, on every subsequent stratum.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1),(2) and Definition 6.8.1; normalized coefficient comparisons of the cited nodes

proof.text: The definition of constructibility in [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] gives a finite locally closed partition $(S_a)$ of $T$ such that $F|_{S_a}$ is pro-etale locally finite free over $E_{S_a}$. The encoding equivalence [def-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-module-encoding], together with the coefficient comparisons of Step 4, regards this as a lisse internal module over the pulled-back condensed $E$ ring. This assertion about lisse objects is justified on the actual trivializing pro-etale cover by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-module-encoding-slice-freeness]; its equivalence is in both directions, including rank zero. This sets up the hypotheses of the internal lattice theorem without identifying internal modules with ordinary sectionwise modules by notation.

source.place: Definition 6.8.6; Definitions 6.8.1, 6.8.3 and the explicit encoding/slice comparison

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-topological-stratified-lisse-lattices] to each of these lisse internal modules on the topologically Noetherian $S_a$. It gives a finite further locally closed partition and, on each member, a lisse internal integral submodule whose ordinary rational scalar extension is the restricted rational module. Under [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] and the ring maps of Step 4 this is a lisse $B_{E,W}$-module lattice $L_W$ with $L_W[1/\varpi]\simeq F|_W$. Here the sectionwise equivalence leaves the underlying sheaf and action unchanged: inverse image applies to that action, and scalar extension is the sheafified quotient of the free bilinear expressions $r\otimes m$ by the balancing relations in both conventions. Thus the identification of inverse images and tensor products is induced by $r\otimes m\mapsto r\otimes m$. It preserves the displayed inclusion and its rationalization. Freeness is checked on the cover by the slice comparison used in Step 5. Replace each member by its reduced locally closed structure. Pullback of the lattice and its localization remains lisse and has the same localization, by the pullback compatibility in [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison]; the rational restriction comparison is that of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization]. Denote this finite refined partition by $(T_\nu)$ and its lattices by $L_\nu$. None of these operations changes $E$.

Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), and Corollary 5.1.5; Weil II (1.1.1)b)-d) via the cited definition

proof.text:
Each $L_
u[0]$ is an integral constructible object by condition (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], since its local model is a finite free $A$-module in degree zero. Its raw rational image is lisse. Under [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] its scalar realization is $L_
u[1/\varpi]$. The PBC realization of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] has the same formula on this integral object and on localized arrows. Its comparison with locally closed pullback identifies $J(M_E|_{T_
u})$ with the object whose image is $F|_{T_
u}$. The isomorphism $L_
u[1/\varpi]\simeq F|_{T_
u}$ from Step 6 therefore lifts, by full faithfulness of this equivalence, to an isomorphism of raw rational objects. The identity-on-integral $J$ transports it back to the sf convention. This proves that the classical system of Step 7 realizes $M_E|_{T_
u}$ by the specified lisse realization, and hence realizes $M|_{T_
u}$ after extending to $\Qlb$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3) and Proposition 6.8.14(2); prescribed scalar realizations, with Proposition 6.8.4

proof.text: For two classical systems with lattices on a stratum, [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] identifies their integral maps with compatible maps of the normalized reduction towers and identifies their rational Hom groups fully faithfully with maps between the localized lisse module sheaves. Combining this with [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] gives full faithfulness into the raw lisse heart. At $\Qlb$ choose a common finite stage for the two objects; the Hom groups on both sides are the directed colimits described in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] and [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], so the finite-stage bijections give a bijection on these colimits. Further locally closed pullback and finite coefficient extension commute with this realization: the first cited comparison asserts this for reduction, limit and localization, and the second asserts it for the raw lisse realization. Their maps are the quotient, balanced tensor and pulled-back basis maps. Thus their composite is the same normalized comparison, also for successive restrictions and field extensions.

At a geometric point the maps of Step 3 identify the finite reductions and the point evaluation, hence their localized fibres. On a lisse stratum [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres] identifies the PBC fibre with $(\varprojlim_n (L_{\nu,n})_{\bar x})\otimes_A E$ and then scalar extension to $\Qlb$. On the sf side [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] identifies this same fibre and carries restriction-and-coprojection transport along a point automorphism to the identical transport in the module model, including every iterate. This proves the adic fibre and iterated geometric-Frobenius point-transport assertions for $J$ and the classical realization.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Proposition 6.8.4; the normalized adic fibre and sf point-transport comparison of the cited nodes

proof.text:
Suppose $T=Y_0	imes_{k_0}k$ and $(M,	heta)$ has a Weil structure as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $V_0$ be a further locally closed piece defined over $k_m$ whose geometric base change $V$ is inside one $T_
u$. Its inclusion $j$ satisfies $g_T^m j=jg_V$; restrict the iterated Weil isomorphism $	heta^{(m)}$ to obtain $g_V^*(M|_V)\simeq M|_V$, using the composition comparisons of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Both objects are lisse by [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] and Step 8. Step 9 lifts this map and its inverse to classical rational lisse maps. Faithfulness sends their two composites to identities, so they are inverse classical maps. The point-transport normalization in Step 10 identifies their local iterated Frobenius maps. If these maps require a larger finite coefficient field, the common-stage Hom definition represents the map, its inverse and the two identity equations at one common finite enlargement. This is a classical lisse Weil isomorphism; it need not preserve the selected integral lattice. Neither $g_T$-stability of the original $T_
u$ nor a Weil structure on $L_
u$ has entered the argument.

source.place: Blueprint thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves.proof.md paragraph 7; normalized lisse comparison and common-stage Weil-pair definition

proof.text: Finally suppose $T=(Y_0\times_{k_0}k)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Apply [lem-zl-smooth-affine-frontier-stratification] to the reduced partition $(T_\nu)$. Its hypotheses are precisely the separated finite-type $Y_0$ and this finite reduced locally closed partition; no initial Frobenius stability is needed. It supplies one $k_m$, the finite reduced closed chain starting at $(Y_0\times_{k_0}k_m)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and all the smooth geometrically connected affine open-and-closed pieces in the successive differences, of constant dimensions $d\geq0$. Their geometric base changes factor as locally closed subschemes through the $T_\nu$. Restrict the already chosen systems and lattices along those factorizations. By [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] and [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization], the restrictions remain lisse, at the same coefficient $E$, with the quotient, coefficient-extension and pullback normalizations already proved. The frontier theorem also gives $U_{a,b}\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k_m$ for a zero-dimensional piece and includes the empty scheme with a length-zero chain. This proves all clauses of the requested refinement.
